# Neighbour-count selection for the k-th-NN attention distance on the validation set
# figure: knn_k_selection
# source: C:\Users\paulk\Desktop\Unistuff\Masterarbeit\Code\PCLA/data/TFV6/val_data_alt
# Generated by figure_notes.py — do not edit; regenerate with the figure.

    BOTH SPLITS since 2026-09-03. Validation solid, test dotted. Validation-only, this figure read as though it contradicted the test-set figures; it does not, it is a different split, and k is selected on the validation curve alone.
    AUROC here is a single pooled AUROC over the FULL validation set INCLUDING Gaussian noise, per k, exactly as run_analysis.py selects k. It is one detector, not a mean over detectors, and it includes Gaussian noise, so it is NOT the criterion used for K in auroc_val_test_vs_K.
    Because the split holds exactly 200 frames of each perturbation and all of them are scored against the same 200 clean frames, a pooled AUROC is identically the unweighted mean of the per-perturbation AUROCs in the pool. Verified to machine precision for every detector. The two are not competing quantities; only the set of perturbations in the pool distinguishes the figures. Here the pool holds all four perturbations.
    'single' scores against the whole 5000-frame baseline. 'GMM' routes each sample to its nearest of the 10 components and scores within that component's pool only, falling back to the full baseline when the pool holds fewer than k frames.
    component sizes ascending: 102, 136, 147, 161, 180, 308, 414, 751, 1010, 1791
    k values exceeding the smallest component: 250  (those k trigger the full-baseline fallback for that component's samples)
    components smaller than k = 100: 0  (of 10)
    components smaller than k = 250: 5  (of 10)

Routing, and how many samples the fallback actually touches
-----------------------------------------------------------
    Counting components exceeded understates the fallback: what matters is how many samples are ROUTED to a component too small for k, since those are scored against a reference set of a different size and therefore on a different scale, mixed into one ranking with the rest.
    baseline frames per component: 0 = 136, 1 = 1791, 2 = 180, 3 = 414, 4 = 161, 5 = 102, 6 = 1010, 7 = 751, 8 = 308, 9 = 147
    validation samples routed to each component: 0 = 103, 1 = 87, 2 = 56, 3 = 3, 4 = 124, 5 = 132, 6 = 154, 7 = 170, 8 = 100, 9 = 71
        component 0: 2.7% of the baseline, 10.3% of the validation samples
        component 1: 35.8% of the baseline, 8.7% of the validation samples
        component 2: 3.6% of the baseline, 5.6% of the validation samples
        component 3: 8.3% of the baseline, 0.3% of the validation samples
        component 4: 3.2% of the baseline, 12.4% of the validation samples
        component 5: 2.0% of the baseline, 13.2% of the validation samples
        component 6: 20.2% of the baseline, 15.4% of the validation samples
        component 7: 15.0% of the baseline, 17.0% of the validation samples
        component 8: 6.2% of the baseline, 10.0% of the validation samples
        component 9: 2.9% of the baseline, 7.1% of the validation samples
    validation samples falling back at k = 250: 486  (48.6%, from 5 component(s))
    Fallback rule, verified in run_analysis.py step 9b.3 (`if len(_pool) < _k: _pool = baseline_series`): the pool is replaced by the FULL baseline. It is not clamped and not padded, and DistanceComputer.compute_knn_distance raises rather than clamping, so the caller is the only place this is handled. Same rule as the Atari implementation.

Selection, and whether it transfers
-----------------------------------
    single: k chosen on validation: 1  (test AUROC there 0.5520)
    single: k that would have won on test: 10  (test AUROC 0.5567, cost of selecting on validation 0.0047)
    gmm: k chosen on validation: 250  (test AUROC there 0.5498)
    gmm: k that would have won on test: 250  (test AUROC 0.5498, cost of selecting on validation 0.0000)
    validation prefers: GMM at k = 250 (0.5932) over single at k = 1 (0.6002)
    test at those same two settings: GMM k = 250: 0.5498, single k = 1: 0.5520  (the selection reverses between the splits)
